summary: TLS-offload proxy normalizes IdP origin (port stripping) and breaks tenant mapping in private deployment
description:
Issue summary: After a recent network change at the customer's on-prem edge (TLS termination moved to a hardware load balancer), several API and Console requests started failing with 403s when users attempted to authenticate via the customer's IdP. Impact: All SAML/OIDC logins that route through the offloading LB intermittently fail tenant resolution and map to the default tenant, causing authorization denial for org-scoped resources. The failures started immediately after the LB change and affect desktop and API clients behind the LB.

Observed failure mode: The customer's LB rewrites the Origin/Host/Audit headers and removes explicit port information (eg. :8443) from the idp-origin header that our private connector expects. The IdP issues assertions where the audience/aud and recipient fields include the original port (8443). When the assertion returns through the LB the stripped origin no longer matches runtime tenant-binding rules and the tenant-aware RBAC lookup falls back to a generic binding that does not include the customer's admin roles.

Why unique: This is not a plain host-rewrite or header-clipping problem; it's a port-normalization mismatch between the IdP's assertion fields and what the private ingress presents to the auth service after TLS offload. Existing tickets have covered header clipping, hostrewrite and trailing-dot edge cases; this one specifically traces to port-stripping during TLS offload and consequent aud/recipient mismatch plus RelayState path differences.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure private connector behind an on-prem LB that terminates TLS and forwards traffic to connector on :8443.
2) Initiate SAML login from customer console.
3) Observe initial redirect to IdP with assertionAudience=https://redwood.internal:8443/sso/consume and RelayState including tenant path.
4) After IdP posts the assertion, LB forwards request but normalizes Origin/Host to https://redwood.internal (removes :8443).
5) Private connector's assertion verifier rejects mapping because aud/recipient mismatch or it maps to default tenant during binding resolution.

Minimal curl reproduction (customer provided):
curl -v -X POST \
  -H "Host: redwood.internal" \
  -H "X-Forwarded-Proto: https" \
  -H "X-Original-Host: redwood.internal:8443" \
  --data-urlencode "SAMLResponse=<base64-assertion>" \
  https://edge-lb.example.com/sso/consume

Expected: Auth flow completes, assertion matches configured SP entity and tenant is resolved to FinSight Analytics tenant.
Actual: Auth flow returns 403 with tenant-mapping fallback and user receives "access denied" for org resources.

comments: 2024-11-20 16:05 - Aditi Rao: Customer reports widespread 403s after LB change; they confirm LB is terminating TLS and forwarding to connector on :8443. Asked for packet capture and assertion sample.

2024-11-20 18:27 - Marcus Chen: Reproduced locally by simulating LB header normalization. When X-Original-Host contains port we accept mapping; when it's absent, tenant resolver falls back. Adding investigation notes and proposed mitigations.

2024-11-21 09:14 - Customer (FinSight SRE): Provided SAMLResponse sample and LB config snippet; they've set 'normalize-request-headers' in firmware. They say enabling preserve-original-host is a config option but requires change window.

2024-11-21 12:40 - Marcus Chen: Confirmed root cause is port stripping. Temporary workaround suggested: enable header preserve on LB (preserve X-Original-Host or include X-Original-Port) or configure connector's SP entity to include both host variants (with and without port). Logged follow-up engineering task INT-881234 to evaluate tolerant aud matching.

2024-11-22 08:50 - Aditi Rao: Customer accepted workaround to preserve X-Original-Host and will apply in maintenance window tomorrow; requested confirmation of config changes required on connector side to support dual-audience acceptance.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: header clipping or host rewrite. Deep dive showed aud/recipient fields in SAML assertion include port 8443. The customer's LB normalizes host to 443 and removes port before forwarding assertion. The connector's tenant resolution does strict aud/recipient matching. We reproduced by toggling X-Original-Host: when present and includes :8443 tenant resolution succeeds; when LB strips port it falls back. No code-level bug in IdP or connector assertion parsing; behavior arises from strict matching policy combined with proxy header normalization. Potential security considerations prevent broadening aud acceptance without explicit config.
Links: Slack thread #support-private (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01SUPP1234/p17110000000000), confluence runbook on SSO-practices (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/SSO+Runbook)
resolution_notes:
Workarounds provided: 1) Recommended LB config change: preserve X-Original-Host including port or add X-Original-Port header. 2) As a short-term connector config change, customer can register SP entity variations that include the asserted port as additional accepted audiences. 3) Engineering task INT-881234 opened to add optional tolerant-audience-mode for private connectors that will accept normalized host variants when enabled and logged.
Status: Customer to apply LB preserve header config in maintenance window; support will validate post-change and then decide whether to enable connector-level tolerant mode. Follow-up: engineering to design audit/tracing for tolerant mode to avoid widening attack surface.
